chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Sudayr al-Sayrafi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, in the Master of this matter there is a resemblance to Yusuf (عليه السلام).” He said: I said to him, “It is as though you are referring to his life or his ghaybah (occultation).”

He said: So he said to me, “And what is there to deny in that? This community is like swine. Indeed, the brothers of Yusuf (عليه السلام) were tribes, the sons of the Prophets. They traded with Yusuf, dealt with him, and spoke to him, while they were his brothers and he was their brother, yet they did not recognize him until he said:”
“I am Yusuf, and this is my brother.”

“So what does this accursed community deny in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, dealing with His hujjah at some time just as He dealt with Yusuf? Indeed, Yusuf (عليه السلام) had the kingdom of Egypt, and between him and his father was a journey of eighteen days. Had he wished to inform him, he would have been able to do so. Ya‘qub (عليه السلام) and his children, upon receiving the good news, traveled nine days from their desert dwelling to Egypt. So what does this community deny in Allah, Majestic and Mighty, dealing with His hujjah just as He dealt with Yusuf: that he may walk in their markets and tread upon their carpets until Allah permits that for him, just as He permitted for Yusuf? They said:”
“Are you indeed Yusuf?” He said: “I am Yusuf.”

key_terms.أَسْوَاقِهِمْ: their markets, indicating ordinary public spaces
key_terms.بُسُطَهُمْ: their carpets or floor coverings, indicating social presence among them
key_terms.حُجَّتِهِ: His divine proof, meaning Allah’s hujjah over creation
key_terms.شَبَهًا: a resemblance or likeness in condition and circumstance
key_terms.صَاحِبِ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرِ: the Master of this matter, referring to the divinely appointed Imam
key_terms.غَيْبَتَهُ: his occultation or absence from open recognition
key_terms.مُلْكُ مِصْرَ: the kingship or authority over Egypt granted to Yusuf

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) compare the ghaybah of the Imam to the story of Yusuf (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a resemblance between the Qa'im, the Master of this matter, and Yusuf (عليه السلام), especially in the sense that he may be present among people while remaining unrecognized until Allah permits his manifest identification. It uses the story of Yusuf (عليه السلام) as a theological and eschatological analogy for the ghaybah of Allah’s hujjah and his eventual disclosure.
